title: When & How to use Git Cherry-Pick
subtitle: Pick specific commits across branches like a Senior Engineer
summary: git cherry-pick allows you to apply a specific commit from one branch onto your current branch without merging the entire history.
key_points: Use Case 1 (Hotfix): You fixed a bug in a development branch and need to port ONLY that fix to the production branch immediately.
Use Case 2 (Accidental Branching): You made a commit on main instead of a feature branch.
Pro Tip: If conflicts occur, resolve them and run 'git cherry-pick --continue', or abort using 'git cherry-pick --abort'.
code_snippet:
# 1. Find the commit hash from git log
git log --oneline
# a1b2c3d Fix payment gateway crash

# 2. Switch to production branch
git checkout main

# 3. Cherry-pick only that commit
git cherry-pick a1b2c3d

complexity.safety: Non-destructive: generates a new SHA hash with the same diff
complexity.best_practice: Use sparingly to avoid duplicate commits in long-lived branches

interview_tip: Interviewers love asking how cherry-pick differs from rebase and merge: merge joins branches, rebase rewrites linear history, cherry-pick copies individual commits.
